For every integer q, expansion gives a fixed discrepancy of 2, an explicit infinite parameter argument.

A generic constant-prime matrix is described and rank-one reasoning is given on the 2x2 witness, but no explicit prime or dimension parameter range is supplied. Whether this natural-language class meets the strict parameterized-family requirement needs adjudication.
The packet defines a cabinet as a pair of independently chosen subsets, gives the corrected product, and explains why addition counts the wrong object.
